criteria.note: One-way and event-driven: grep proved every mutation targets local structures (no file write), only the three WARP-0603 seam write methods are called (no intake reads, so no polling), and a deep before/after compare showed the input spec_index and config unchanged after a full run; the write audit is a subset of the three seam writes.

Status maps onto the tracker's own statuses via status_map; desired is only ever a mapped value, so an unmapped WARP status never transitions (NG4) but is annotated as a keyed comment; empty status_map is comments-only; per-repo override wins. A mutation using status_map.get(ws, ws) turned the NG4 assertion red.

Reconciler idempotency proven under replay, doubled event id, prefix growth, out-of-order-with-timestamps, and replay-after-shipped (no backward drive); state byte-identical, closing comment posts exactly once. No processed-offset ledger and no second store.

Reuse proven by spy: tracker_for_repo resolves to .warp/tracker.py and is actually invoked; no routing or seam reimplementation. All four unwired cases skip by name with mirrored==[]; a malformed status_map (blank value, unknown key, non-string) fails closed by name (MirrorError).

Non-tautology proven by a mutation matrix (neutering set_status -> 4 red; unmapped-transition sneak -> 2 red; closing-comment removal -> 2 red; dedup break -> 1 red; unmapped-annotation removal -> 1 red). The one-way guard was strengthened to a fresh never-mirrored index after the first review found it dull; a re-review confirmed the new guard is red-on-injection, green-clean.

findings.text: Full independent adversarial review at faa579c returned pass_with_notes, 0 blocking, confirming all 5 ACs against the code with spies (proving real reuse of WARP-0601 tracker_for_repo and the WARP-0603 seam, not reading), a mutation matrix, and a full idempotency battery it could not break. It raised three non-blocking notes: a dull one-way teeth guard (the assertion reused an already-mirrored index), a dead import os, and an unreachable out-of-order-without-timestamps robustness edge (the real emitter always stamps at and reads in emission order).

The two actionable notes were FIXED in this commit (9bbfc5a): the dead import removed and the one-way guard rewritten to a fresh, never-mirrored index that demonstrably catches a stable-value writeback (mutation-verified: red on a planted meta[status]=desired, green clean). The unreachable robustness edge was accepted as not reachable via the real event emitter. A scoped independent re-review bound to 9bbfc5a returned PASS with zero findings: the delta is exactly the two fixes with the mirror logic byte-unchanged (mirror_events, resolve_status_map, _child_identity byte-identical between commits), the gate is GREEN at 9bbfc5a (selftest 1133 passed, 0 failed), and the two capabilities.yaml copies remain byte-identical.

Operational: built in-session by a single writer after the subagent build worker died on the shared session token limit at 2pm (not a WARP defect). Serialized single-writer discipline was kept throughout; the commit was verified GREEN in a clean detached worktree before and after the review fixes. No template twin ships for tracker_mirror.py (not a validate.py/policy_check.py load dependency), matching tracker_adapter.py; check_template_sync is unchanged.

summary: W5 of PLAN-0006 (the event-driven one-way spec mirror) is correct. Two independent adversarial reviews (a full pass on faa579c, a scoped re-review bound to this shipped commit 9bbfc5a) both PASS with 0 blocking. The mirror is a reconciler that projects spec lifecycle events onto a tracker child's status and closing comment, one-directionally: it writes only status and comments through the WARP-0603 seam, never a spec or plan definition, and never mutates its input index (the repository stays the single source of truth). It is idempotent under at-least-once delivery by construction (recompute the desired state each run; set_status no-ops when unchanged; comments are keyed) with no processed-offset ledger and no second store, and it never invents a transition outside the mapped status set (NG4). It reuses WARP-0601 (tracker_for_repo) and the WARP-0603 seam with no reimplementation, skips unwired specs by name, and fails closed on a malformed status_map. Gate GREEN (selftest 1133 passed, 0 failed), no regression, no protected path. proof_digest via validate.py over {spec_id, commit, criteria, checks}.
